needs.what: Play the v2 milestones that are merged on the play server
needs.why: Nobody played them yet; the defaults below shape them

needs.what: Answer cards Q21 to Q37 or leave the defaults
needs.why: Each default is reversible; changing one before its milestone is cheapest

decisions.title: Continue or restart?
decisions.ruling: Continue; v1 scope M0 to M4 approved (2026-11-02).

decisions.title: Gold and gems value?
Delete superseded branches and untrack old tool configs?
decisions.ruling: Yes, including the push to origin.

decisions.title: v3 nation AI: scripted, LLM or both?
Who merges a milestone PR?
decisions.context: Low involvement versus your usual PR review. With agent merge you watch this page and can revert; with your merge each milestone waits for you.
decisions.suggestion: Settled 2026-11-09 (NR-012): the agent merges once the gate and the milestone review are green.

decisions.title: Run milestones without ultracode workflows?
decisions.context: Your profile says coding runs as ultracode (build, review, verify per task). In the work repo, review and verify agents were 32% of spend and follow-up rounds 10%.
decisions.suggestion: Settled 2026-11-09 (NR-013): no ultracode workflows unless one is expected to improve the result by far.

decisions.title: Use NotebookLM over gameplay videos to close rules gaps?
decisions.context: Videos can show on-screen values: university, armoury and shipyard costs, starting state, power plant, score screen, relationship levels; partly price series and job durations. They cannot show hidden formulas (trade-partner weighting, credit, combat, council, AI).
decisions.suggestion: Settled 2026-11-09 (NR-014): no NotebookLM; agents search the web for screenshots themselves and follow Imperialism (1997).

decisions.title: Rail on hills, swamp and mountains before a technology shop exists?
decisions.context: The rules sell these three technologies; v1 cannot buy technology, so rail stopped at the first hill.
decisions.suggestion: Settled 2026-11-09 (NR-015): every nation starts with the three rail technologies until technology can be bought.

decisions.title: Freight cars: usable this turn or next turn?
decisions.context: The rules say a freight car bought now carries goods next turn. The code lets it carry this turn (FR-039), which feels more responsive but differs from the original.
decisions.suggestion: Settled 2026-11-09 (NR-016): as the original. Orders are chosen and changeable during the turn and apply at End Turn; a freight car carries goods from the next turn. Changed in M4.

decisions.title: Should a new migrant also cost cash?
decisions.context: The rules charge canned food, clothing and furniture for a migrant, no cash. M3 follows that.
decisions.suggestion: Settled 2026-11-09 (NR-017): as the original. Migrant = canned food + clothing + furniture, no cash; training 00 + 1 paper, then ,000 + 2 paper.

decisions.title: Score weights?
decisions.context: Score = 1 point per $100 + 10 per building capacity point + 10 per resource level on own tiles. An idle game scores 250, all from the starting assets.
decisions.suggestion: Settled 2026-11-09 (NR-018): keep the weights for v1.

decisions.title: Game length?
decisions.context: The game ends after 40 turns (Winter 1824). The original ends on a vote of the Council of Governors, which v1 does not have.
decisions.suggestion: Settled 2026-11-03: 40 turns in v1; the Council of Governors vote is recorded as NR-011 for v2.

decisions.title: Price model?
decisions.context: Prices move each turn by a seeded random step up to 3% plus 0.5% per net unit traded (cap 3%), bounded 50% to 250% of start. The review found a small built-in profit: buy, let your own buying push the price up, sell next turn (about $72 per two turns on $900 goods).
decisions.suggestion: Settled 2026-11-09 (NR-018): keep for v1, fix the self-push in v2.

decisions.title: Should cargo holds limit trade?
decisions.context: Each unit traded uses one hold; a nation has 4 holds and cannot add more in v1 (no shipyard yet).
decisions.suggestion: Settled 2026-11-09 (NR-018): keep the 4-hold limit.

decisions.title: Should trade orders repeat every turn?
decisions.context: Today trade orders last one turn, so the player re-enters them each turn. A repeat button was skipped as not trivial.
decisions.suggestion: Settled 2026-11-09 (NR-018): one-turn orders; repeat button only if play feels tedious.

decisions.title: How should the computer nation score better?
decisions.context: The new scripted player lays a few rail lines and builds depots as asked (NR-022). It ships far more (268 vs 181 units at turn 15) but scores slightly lower (382 vs 390), because extra goods sit unsold: 4 cargo holds cap sales at 32 units and stock is not scored.
decisions.suggestion: Settled 2026-11-10: improve the score now. Done in M4.2 (NR-023): the computer scores 1.6 to 2.5 times the M4 player.

decisions.title: Where should recruited and trained workers appear?
decisions.context: v1 creates no civilians after the start; recruits and trained workers join the industry workforce, and there is no University. The start civilians stay on the capital tile (rules 03).
decisions.suggestion: Settled 2026-11-12 (NR-029): leave it until a University or another civilian-producing rule exists.

decisions.title: How should the score treat idle building capacity?
decisions.context: After M4.2 the computer nation scores about 1,650 at turn 40 (idle human: 240). 1,080 of those points are building capacity; about 87% of it cannot run, because 7 workers give 28 labour (at most 14 units a turn) against 108 capacity points. The computer never recruits workers.
decisions.suggestion: Answered 2026-11-12: let the computer recruit. Measured in M4.4: even free workers lower its score (labour is not the limit; inputs and freight cars are). See card Q21.

decisions.title: Hide the Materials and Goods groups in the transport popup until something produces them?
decisions.context: In v1 all materials and goods show 0 / 0 in the transport popup, and the rules say some (paper, canned food, armaments) can never be shipped.
decisions.suggestion: Settled 2026-11-12 (NR-027): done in M4.4; empty groups are hidden.

decisions.title: Should the computer recruit workers at all?
decisions.context: Measured in M4.4: with free workers (upper bound) the computer scores 2972 to 5513 against 5925 without, summed over four seeds at turn 40. The best real policy (R2) grows the workforce 7 to 9 and costs about 350 points (6%), margin still 1.57. About 28% of labour is idle; from turn 20 freight cars limit shipping. More cars alone gave +86 (1.4%).
decisions.suggestion: (a) No recruiting in v1 (taken meanwhile); revisit with (c) transport and inputs first when we plan v2 AI work.

decisions.title: Should the v2 world have one land-bridge minor nation and three island minors?
decisions.context: Two land bridges put Valdoria's capital province next to a minor nation (one battle from a capital rush); one bridge keeps both capitals behind other provinces. Options: (a) two bridges; (b) one bridge, three islands; (c) mirrored islands (breaks tile ids). Found in the M5 review: Arvelia's and Lorran's capitals are one step nearer Testland than Valdoria (a small tilt toward the human).
decisions.suggestion: (b) taken: Arvelia bridges the north; Sundmark, Lorran and Pellis are islands (trade only until ships). The tilt is accepted for now; a fix is a 3-tile Lorran centred at 12-1 under a new requirement. Default in force; reversible.

decisions.title: Should each minor nation be one province?
decisions.context: The original has 16 minors of 4 provinces; the 24x16 map fits 4 small ones. (a) one province: a war on a minor is one battle; (b) two provinces each: two battles; (c) a bigger map.
decisions.suggestion: (a) taken; revisit after play. Default in force; reversible.

decisions.title: Should relations move by 10 points a level (+1 a trade, +2 to +8 a grant, +10 a pact, -40 a war)?
decisions.context: No source states the 1997 step sizes; the wiki ladder (about 150 trades to the top) is out of reach in 40 turns.
decisions.suggestion: Taken: about 50 trades or grants from yellow to dark green. Default in force; reversible.

decisions.title: Should both Great Powers start equal with every minor (yellow) and with each other (beige, embassies)?
decisions.context: The original makes minors friendlier to the computer on Normal.
decisions.suggestion: Equal start taken. Default in force; reversible.

decisions.title: Should trading with a minor nation need a consulate?
decisions.context: 1997 rule: anyone can trade; a consulate only makes deals raise relations. The plan rule makes the $500 consulate the first strategic choice.
decisions.suggestion: Consulate needed (plan rule) taken; easy to switch. Default in force; reversible.

decisions.title: Should a minor offer 1 unit per resource tile (at most 6) and buy 2 of each good a turn?
decisions.context: Matches observed 1997 offers (1 to 6 units); demand growth over time is unknown (gap C5).
decisions.suggestion: Taken. Default in force; reversible.

decisions.title: Should the favourite partner rank by relation points plus half the subsidy percent, with deals at the shown board price?
decisions.context: 1997 settles at a clearing price unknown when ordering; the default lets the player know the price in advance.
decisions.suggestion: Taken. Default in force; reversible.

decisions.title: Should the computer accept an alliance at level 7 of 9 and peace when it is losing?
decisions.context: A 1997 guide says AI hatred never stops; the default gives a predictable opponent.
decisions.suggestion: Taken. Default in force; reversible.

decisions.title: Should each Great Power start with 2 Regulars, 1 Artillery, militia and a fort on its capital?
decisions.context: Gives each side enough to take a minor nation early; upkeep $100 a turn like the 1815 ledger.
decisions.suggestion: Taken. Default in force; reversible.

decisions.title: Should regiment costs not seen on a screen (Hussars, Cuirassiers, Light Artillery, Grenadiers) use derived values, and Sappers be left out?
decisions.context: Only Skirmishers ($200) and Artillery ($1,000) costs are confirmed on screenshots.
decisions.suggestion: Derived costs taken, no Sappers. Default in force; reversible.

decisions.title: Should battles use simple numbers (8 rounds, 70% hit, rout at 25 health) with defenders fully visible?
decisions.context: The 1997 combat formulas are unknown; simple numbers are testable and the battle screen replays them.
decisions.suggestion: Taken. Default in force; reversible.

decisions.title: Should a country have at most one army per province (no merge order)?
decisions.context: Named armies with merge and split add about 3 orders and screens.
decisions.suggestion: One army per province taken. Default in force; reversible.

decisions.title: Should taking a Great Power capital give all its provinces to the winner, and taking a minor capital make it a colony?
decisions.context: In 1997 a fallen power falls into anarchy and fights on.
decisions.suggestion: Taken (simpler, ends a 2-power game). Default in force; reversible.

decisions.title: Should the computer go to war with the weakest minor from turn 10 when it is twice as strong, never with a Great Power?
decisions.context: It makes the computer compete for minors without threatening the score baselines.
decisions.suggestion: Taken. Default in force; reversible.

decisions.title: When upkeep cannot be paid, should the newest regiments be disbanded?
decisions.context: v2 has no credit rule (gap A8).
decisions.suggestion: Taken. Default in force; reversible.

decisions.title: Should a grant to the other Great Power give it the money?
decisions.context: In M6 a grant takes the money from the giver and no country receives it; it only raises relations. The 1997 rule is not documented.
decisions.suggestion: Taken: nobody receives it (a pure relations cost). Default in force; reversible.

decisions.title: Should Join the Empire, rail and sea moves, generals and medals stay out of v2?
decisions.context: Each adds orders and screens; colonies come only by conquest meanwhile.
decisions.suggestion: Taken (later milestone). Default in force; reversible.

decisions.title: Should prices on the partners market move only with the Great Powers' own deals, with no pull back toward the start price?
decisions.context: Before the review fix round the minors' fixed demand (24 goods a turn) and offers counted as excess demand, so goods ran to the 250% ceiling (clothing $2,250 by turn 35) and raw to the 50% floor by turn 30 whatever the players did. Now (FR-243) a price moves with the units the Great Powers bought minus the units they sold, as on the v1 world market. Measured at turn 40, seeds 1 to 4: clothing $648 to $710 (v1 world: $642), timber $144 to $180 (both computers buy it), no price at a bound. A nation that keeps buying or selling one commodity can still push it to a bound in time.
decisions.suggestion: Taken: Great Powers' deals only (FR-243). Alternative: a pull of about 10% a turn back toward the start price, so a constant push settles near 1.4 times the start; say if you want it.

decisions.title: Should the v2 trade baseline count the minors per nation or for both nations together?
decisions.context: FR-196 said "deals with at least 2 minors" without saying whose. Since the review fix round the computer opens a consulate only with a minor it will use (FR-245): nation 1 deals with all 4 minors, nation 2 only with Arvelia (Arvelia favours it and covers its 4 holds). A per-nation minimum would make the computer pay $500 for consulates it does not use.
decisions.suggestion: Taken: both nations together, at least 2 minors; each nation at least 1 minor and at least 1 purchase (FR-247).

decisions.title: Should the computer buy raw materials from minors, and open a consulate only where it will trade?
decisions.context: FR-193 had the computer bid only for lumber and steel, which no minor sells, so it never bought in "partners" and paid $2,000 for four consulates it used once. FR-245: it bids for the timber, coal, iron ore and cotton its mills lack (capped at what its partner minors offer), and orders a consulate only when the minors that favour it do not cover its holds. Score at turn 40 against the same player without raw bids, both nations summed: +82, +94, +25 and -20 (seeds 1 to 4).
decisions.suggestion: Taken (FR-245). Reversible; FR-247 pins its numbers.

decisions.title: Should a "world" market keep the v1 shape, with no mode key?
decisions.context: M7 engine decision 1: two-islands keeps its v1 market object (FR-060's assertion unchanged); a market without a mode is read as "world" through marketModeOf (FR-242).
decisions.suggestion: Taken. Default in force.

decisions.title: Should the engine give the Deal Book as data and the screen write the words?
decisions.context: M7 engine decision 3: dealBook returns entries; the ledger lines ("Sold 1 Clothing to Arvelia @ $810") come from the screen's dealBookView, beside the other display names (FR-244). A v3 player that reads text would want the words from the engine.
decisions.suggestion: Taken: data in the engine, words in the screen. Revisit for v3.

decisions.title: When the computer offers goods, should it count each minor's whole demand, not what the rival may sell there first?
decisions.context: M7 engine decision 7: its offers are capped at its partner minors' whole demand this turn; it cannot see the rival's offers (FR-245 (c)). An unsold unit comes back to the warehouse at no cost.
decisions.suggestion: Taken. Default in force.

decisions.title: Should the market e2e test sell a furniture to a minor, now that nobody buys lumber?
decisions.context: M7 UI decision 3: in "partners" nobody buys lumber, so the FR-078 e2e orders a consulate with Pellis and sells 1 furniture on turn 2, reading the income from the news instead of a fixed $300.
decisions.suggestion: Taken. Default in force.

decisions.title: Should a Board of Trade button the engine would refuse be disabled with its reason?
decisions.context: M7 UI decision 4 kept the v1 way (press, then read "Purchase refused: over the limit."). The review asked for the M6 way: the "+" is disabled and its title says why: "No free hold this turn", "Already 4 bids this turn, the most", "None left in the warehouse", "Not enough money" (FR-248).
decisions.suggestion: Done in the review fix round (FR-248).

decisions.title: Should the World market also drop its greyed "−" at 0, as the Board of Trade does?
decisions.context: QA item 7 (every disabled control says why) was applied to the Board of Trade only (FR-257: at 0 there is no "−", only its place). The World market, shown in a "world" game such as two-islands, keeps the v1 stepper: a greyed "−" at 0 with no reason (FR-074, pinned by tests/ui/marketDialog.test.tsx and tests/ui/boardOfTrade.test.tsx). Changing it is one line in MarketModal.tsx (hideLessAtZero) plus FR-074, FR-257 and those two tests.
decisions.suggestion: Yes, one stepper for both market dialogs. Until answered the v1 stepper stays (FR-257 as written).
